task: Social media user influence network analysis (2-source username join -> per-user aggregation -> directed weighted graph -> PageRank)

columns.name: User ID
columns.role: id (NOT a stable user key, see risks)

columns.name: Follower Count
columns.role: primary metric for edge sampling weights

files.note: No mention/follower columns; only Retweets/Likes/Tweet_ID. Text contains no '@' mentions (0 rows), so mention counts cannot be derived from text.

join.key: Username matched case-insensitively (str.strip().str.lower()); User ID must NOT be used: 6035 usernames map to >1 User ID
join.data_quality: no leading/trailing whitespace, no embedded spaces, no non-alphanumeric chars, no mixed-case usernames in either file; lowering case produces no intra-file collisions -> case-insensitive join is safe/clean

aggregation_notes.mention_count: only in bot_detection_data.csv ('Mention Count'); rows sum 0-5. Per-user choice needed: sum vs max vs mean (mean/sum differ for the 6035 users with >1 row).
aggregation_notes.follower_count: only in bot_detection_data.csv; 6033 users have >1 distinct follower value across their rows (average spread), so sum/max/mean differ.
aggregation_notes.engagement: twitter_dataset contributes Retweets/Likes only; overlap users: 2694 users / 3095 rows. Use these as supplementary engagement metrics if a combined score is wanted.

graph_construction_implications.node_set: decision needed: union (47319 users) vs inner join (2694 users). Inner join = only users present in both sources.
graph_construction_implications.out_degree: min(mention_count, 10) incoming edges per target user; Mention Count max per row = 5, per-user sum max = 69 (overlap) -> cap of 10 actually binds only for heavy multi-row users.
graph_construction_implications.edge_probability: source user sampled from other users with probability proportional to follower_count (Follower Count ranges 0-10000, skew moderate: mean ~4989, no all-zero-follower user among overlap).
graph_construction_implications.weighting: edge weight appears intended = target user's mention count (or mention count / edges); state explicitly downstream.
graph_construction_implications.pagerank_spec: networkx.pagerank(G, alpha=0.85, weight='weight') on the directed weighted graph
graph_construction_implications.reproducibility: random.seed(42) / numpy default_rng(42) before sampling edges; sampling order must be deterministic (sort nodes) to guarantee identical output across runs.

risks: User ID is not unique per username (6035 usernames have multiple IDs) -> aggregate by username only.
Follower Count and Mention Count are row-level in the bot file; different aggregation choices change PageRank ranks -> document the choice in the output.
Only 2694 of 9447 twitter users (28.5%) exist in the bot file; if inner join is used, ~6753 users are dropped.
Follower count has 4 zero-valued rows; weight-proportional sampling must guard against zero total weight / division by zero.
Several users have mention_count aggregated 0 -> zero out-degree; PageRank needs a dangling-node handling (networkx handles automatically) and results must not be NaN.
Output requires pagerank rounded to 6 dp plus mention_count and follower_count columns, so the chosen per-user aggregation must be final before writing output.csv.
